div.head: II Cn 76
div.ab: And gyf hwylc man forstolen þingc ham to his cotan bringe ⁊ he arasod wurðe, riht is, þæt he hæbbe þæt he æftereode.
And gif hwilc man forstolen þingc ham to his cotan bringe ⁊ he arasod wurðe, riht is, þæt he habbe þæt he æftereode.
Si homo furtiuum aliquid in domo sua occultabit et ita fuerit arased (abarnatus), rectum est, ut habeat quod quesiuit.
Be forstolene æhta. Gyf hwa forstolen ðingc ham to his coton bringe ⁊ he arefned wyrðe, riht is þæt he hæbbe þæt he æftereode.
And gyf hwylc man forstolen þingc ham to his cotan bringe and he arasod wurðe, riht is þæt he hæbbe þæt he æftereode.
(Von gestohlener Fahrhabe. B) Und wenn jemand eine gestohlene Sache heim in seine Hütte bringt und er wird ertappt, so ist Recht, dass der [Eigenthümer] das erhalte, dem er [spürend] nachging.
(Of stolen goods. B) And if anyone brings a stolen thing home to his cottage and he is caught, it is right that [the owner] should have what he [tracking] went after.
Concerning stolen goods. If anyone carries stolen goods home to his cottage and is detected, the law is that he (the owner) shall have what he has tracked.
And if any man brings home stolen property to his cottage, and he is found out, it is right that he [the owner] should have what he has tracked.
And if anyone brings stolen goods back to his home and is discovered, the law is that the finder shall have that which he has found.
